context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and provides case management tools for analysts. It processes 3,000 transactions per second for a mid-size payment processor in AWS eu-west-1.

## Key Elements
* Shopper / Cardholder and Merchant / Payment Gateway (External entities)
* Fraud Analyst (Internal user)
* API Gateway / Load Balancer (AWS ALB)
* Fraud Scoring Service (AWS ECS Fargate containers)
* Case Management UI & Service (AWS ECS Fargate containers)
* In-Memory Feature Cache & Model Store (AWS ElastiCache Redis)
* Audit Pipeline (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and AWS S3 with Object Lock)
* Identity and Access Management (AWS Cognito)

## Relationships
* Merchants connect to API Gateway via gRPC/TLS for real-time scoring.
* Fraud Analysts access Case Management UI via HTTPS/TLS authenticated by AWS Cognito.
* Fraud Scoring Service queries local in-memory features and AWS ElastiCache Redis over TCP.
* Fraud Scoring Service publishes audit events asynchronously to Amazon Kinesis.
* Amazon Kinesis persists audit logs to AWS S3 Object Lock.

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for blue/green zero-downtime deployments without operational overhead.
* AWS ElastiCache Redis: Low-latency caching for real-time feature lookup meeting <50ms P99 SLA.
* Amazon Kinesis & S3: Asynchronous decoupling for tamper-evident 7-year audit retention within budget.
* AWS Cognito: Managed authentication supporting PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to remain maintainable by a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Asynchronous logging and local caching isolate critical scoring paths to reliably achieve sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors to detect fraud. It provides sub-50ms automated decisions and case management tools for fraud analysts while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
* Shopper / Cardholder and Merchant / Payment Gateway (External Actors)
* Fraud Analyst, Risk Operations Manager, and Fraud Model Data Scientist (Internal Users)
* AWS ALB / API Gateway (Ingress)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Stateless Go service on Amazon ECS Fargate with pre-warmed tasks)
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) (Feature Store and cache)
* Case Management & Analytics API (Backend service)
* Frontend Web App (React SPA for analysts and risk managers)
* Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Case management and application database)
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS (Tamper-evident audit log storage)
* AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS (Asynchronous event processing)

## Relationships
* Merchant Payment Gateway to AWS ALB via HTTPS
* AWS ALB to Real-Time Scoring Engine via HTTP/2
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) via RESP
* Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon S3 via HTTPS for tamper-evident audit logging
* Frontend Web App to Case Management & Analytics API via HTTPS
* Case Management & Analytics API to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL via TCP/SQL

## Technology Stack
* AWS (Cloud Provider, region eu-west-1): Chosen to satisfy enterprise reliability and infrastructure constraints.
* Go: Selected for the Real-Time Scoring Engine to ensure high concurrency and sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
* Amazon ECS (Fargate): Used with pre-warmed tasks to prevent cold-start latency spikes within budget.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides ultra-low latency access to feature vectors.
* Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Manages persistent relational data for case management.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Ensures immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit logs for PCI-DSS compliance.
* Terraform: Enables infrastructure-as-code management operable by a 3-engineer team.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict sub-50ms P99 decision latency at 3,000 TPS using pre-warmed Go containers and Redis while incorporating a circuit breaker for fail-safe availability. It maintains a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operates within 3-engineer limits by relying on fully managed AWS serverless services.

AWS ALB / API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS (eu-west-1) for a mid-size payment processor and provides case management for fraud analysts. It operates within a €25,000/month budget, satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and maintains sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.

## Key Elements
- Merchant / Payment Gateway (External System)
- Shopper / Cardholder (External User)
- Fraud Analyst (Internal User)
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) with AWS WAF (Ingress Container)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, Amazon ECS Fargate Container)
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis (Cache Container)
- Case Management & Analytics API (Backend Container)
- Frontend Web App (React SPA Container)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Database Container)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS, Amazon S3 Glacier (Storage Containers)
- AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS (Messaging Containers)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> AWS ALB: Sends payment authorizations [HTTPS / HTTP/2]
- AWS ALB -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes scoring requests [HTTP/2 / VPC Lattice]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine <-> Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Evaluates rules and models [Redis Protocol]
- Fraud Analyst -> AWS ALB: Accesses review workflows [HTTPS]
- AWS ALB -> Frontend Web App: Serves static SPA assets [HTTPS]
- AWS ALB -> Case Management & Analytics API: Routes management traffic [HTTPS]
- Case Management & Analytics API -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Persists cases and audit trails [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3: Stores tamper-evident decision logs [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
- AWS ALB -> Amazon S3: Stores AWS WAF and ALB access logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) & AWS WAF: Provides high-throughput Layer 7 ingress, TLS 1.3 termination, and volumetric attack mitigation within budget.
- Go on Amazon ECS Fargate: Delivers sub-50ms P99 decision latency with minimal compute resource overhead.
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Enables low-latency in-memory feature caching for real-time scoring.
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational storage for structured case management data and audit logs.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Tamper-evident, encrypted storage ensuring the 7-year audit retention requirement (R-06).
- Terraform: Infrastructure as Code tool managed by a 3-engineer team, validated via automated security checks (`tflint`, `checkov`).

## Rationale
The architecture pairs a high-throughput, single-ALB ingress with Go-based ECS Fargate services to hit the strict 50ms P99 latency SLA at 3,000 TPS. Consolidating components onto managed AWS services ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while respecting the €25,000 monthly budget and operational constraints of a three-engineer team.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real time while providing case management and auditability. It processes authorizations with sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS on AWS within a €25,000 monthly budget.]

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst and Risk Manager / Data Scientist
* AWS ALB / API Gateway
* Real-Time Scoring Engine container (Go, Amazon ECS Fargate)
* API Handler Component, Feature Aggregator Component, Scoring Evaluator Component, Audit Logger Component, Fallback Circuit Breaker Component
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS
* AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS

## Relationships
* AWS ALB / API Gateway -> API Handler Component: Routes HTTP/2 scoring requests
* Feature Aggregator Component -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves real-time feature vectors via RESP
* Audit Logger Component -> AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS: Batch-streams decision payloads via HTTPS
* Audit Logger Component -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Writes tamper-evident logs via HTTPS
* Fallback Circuit Breaker Component -> Scoring Evaluator Component: Manages in-memory fallback routing states locally

## Technology Stack
* Go / net/http: High-performance, memory-efficient runtime for API handling and scoring
* Amazon ECS Fargate: Container orchestration with pre-provisioned baseline tasks to handle 3,000 TPS under budget
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory data store for ultra-low latency feature retrieval
* AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS: Asynchronous messaging to decouple audit logging from the critical path
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Tamper-evident, cryptographically secured 7-year audit log storage

## Rationale
[This architecture uses containerized Go components and in-memory Redis caching to consistently achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Asynchronous Kinesis batching and an in-memory fallback circuit breaker ensure PCI-DSS compliance and high availability within budget for a three-person engineering team.]

Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations and manages fraud analyst reviews. It provides sub-50ms fraud decisions while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Shopper / Cardholder & Merchant / Payment Gateway (External Users and Systems)
- Frontend Web App (React SPA)
- Case Management & Analytics API (Backend service)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) (Feature store and cache)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Primary relational database)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS (Tamper-evident audit logs and backups)
- AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS (Event streaming)
- AWS ALB / API Gateway (Ingress management)

## Relationships
- Shopper / Merchant -> AWS ALB / API Gateway: Submits payment authorizations over HTTPS / gRPC
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves transient feature vectors via RESP (TLS 1.2+)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Reads fraud rules and writes audit logs via SQL/TLS
- Fraud Analyst -> Frontend Web App: Reviews suspicious payments over HTTPS
- Frontend Web App -> Case Management & Analytics API: Manages review cases over HTTPS / JSON

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for zero-server-management overhead by a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory feature store using Redis Hashes for O(1) lookups under 50ms P99 latency.
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational store for rules and cases, supporting ACID compliance.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Provides immutable 7-year audit retention required for compliance.
- AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest across data stores for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Rationale
This AWS-centric serverless and managed-service architecture keeps operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It leverages Redis for sub-50ms P99 decision latency and multi-AZ deployments with S3 Object Lock to guarantee PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

Case Management & Analytics API.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management & Analytics API processes fraud investigation workflows and reporting for analysts and risk managers. It enforces PCI-DSS compliance and sub-50ms latency while maintaining immutable 7-year audit logs on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Primary users)
- Frontend Web App (React SPA)
- Case Management & Analytics API (NestJS backend service)
- REST/GraphQL Handler with Data Masking Middleware
- Case Service and Analytics Query Engine
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Primary (OLTP) and Read Replica (OLAP)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Frontend Web App -> REST/GraphQL Handler: API requests [HTTPS]
- REST/GraphQL Handler -> Case Service: Transactional state updates [In-Memory / TCP]
- Case Service -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Primary: Case reads and writes [TCP/SQL]
- Analytics Query Engine -> Amazon RDS Read Replica: Reporting queries [TCP/SQL]
- Audit Logger -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Immutable audit records [HTTPS via AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js with NestJS: Chosen for rapid API development with a 3-engineer team
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Provides transactional persistence with CQRS Read Replica for OLAP isolation
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit log retention for PCI-DSS

Amazon RDS PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management tools for fraud analysts. It is operated by a three-engineer team under strict budget and compliance constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst
- Shopper / Cardholder
- Merchant / Payment Gateway
- AWS ALB / API Gateway
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Case Management & Analytics API
- Frontend Web App (React SPA)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Case Management Schema, Audit & Explainability Log, Partition Manager, Data Purge & TTL Worker)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS
- AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS
- AWS Lambda
- PgBouncer / Amazon RDS Proxy

## Relationships
- Case Management & Analytics API -> Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Reads and writes active cases and audit logs [TCP/TLS/SQL]
- Partition Manager -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Offloads expired partitions [HTTPS]
- AWS Lambda -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Archives data partitions [HTTPS]
- Frontend Web App -> Case Management & Analytics API: Manages review cases [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Relational database with `pg_partman` for structured data storage and partitioning.
- AWS Lambda: Serverless compute for running automated data archival pipelines.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Immutable, encrypted storage for 7-year audit retention.
- PgBouncer / Amazon RDS Proxy: Connection pooling to prevent database connection exhaustion.
- TLS 1.3: Network transport security protocol for strict PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses automated partitioning and S3 archiving to maintain sub-50ms query performance while complying with 7-year audit rules under a 25,000 EUR budget. Schema decomposition and connection pooling ensure high availability and security for a three-engineer team.

## Overview
[A real-time payment fraud screening system for a mid-size payment processor that evaluates card-not-present transactions for fraud and provides case management for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, maintains 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and operates within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Shopper / Cardholder (External System)
- Merchant / Payment Gateway (External System)
- AWS ALB / API Gateway (Container)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Container - Go, Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) (Container)
- Case Management & Analytics API (Container - Backend service)
- Frontend Web App (Container - React SPA)
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (Container)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS (Container)
- AWS Kinesis Data Streams (Container - Real-Time Payment Event Stream)
- Amazon SQS (Container - Asynchronous Task Queue)

## Relationships
- Shopper / Cardholder interacts with Merchant / Payment Gateway via HTTPS/TLS
- Merchant / Payment Gateway sends authorization requests to AWS ALB / API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
- AWS ALB / API Gateway forwards requests to Real-Time Scoring Engine via HTTP/REST
- Real-Time Scoring Engine ingests streaming data from AWS Kinesis Data Streams via HTTPS (AWS SDK GetRecords)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine publishes audit logs and review cases to Amazon SQS via HTTPS (AWS SDK SendMessage)
- Case Management & Analytics API consumes tasks from Amazon SQS via HTTPS (AWS SDK ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage)
- Frontend Web App communicates with Case Management & Analytics API via HTTPS/JSON

## Technology Stack
- AWS (Cloud Provider, eu-west-1 region): Chosen for robust compliance frameworks and managed services matching the 3-engineer team constraint.
- Go on Amazon ECS Fargate: Selected for the Real-Time Scoring Engine to meet the <50ms P99 latency requirement at high throughput.
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Used for transactional case management data storage.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Chosen to meet strict 7-year tamper-evident auditability mandates (R-06).
- AWS Kinesis Data Streams (On-Demand) & Amazon SQS (Standard/FIFO): Used for scalable real-time ingestion and asynchronous task processing without manual operational overhead.
- React SPA: Provides a responsive user interface for fraud analysts.

## Rationale
[This AWS serverless and container-based architecture meets strict sub-50ms latency SLAs and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Utilizing managed services like ECS Fargate, SQS, and Kinesis On-Demand minimizes operational toil, enabling a three-engineer team to reliably operate, scale, and audit the system.]
